problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-1,{e}^{2t+5}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,2{e}^{2t+5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,4{e}^{2t+5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
